paragraphs: During World War II, the museum building was damaged, and the museum collection suffered significant losses.

According to research by Liudmila Yeromina, 3,414 exhibits were removed from the collection during the Romanian occupation, including a significant number of valuable antique pieces of furniture. A 1942 document regarding the transfer of museum items to the Romanian administration has also been preserved, specifically stained-glass windows “depicting saints.” However, available sources do not provide sufficient grounds to unequivocally link this document to the stained-glass windows above the staircase to the second floor that were lost during World War II.

In 1944, an explosion in the Port of Odesa damaged the eastern column of the south portal, the corner of the pediment, and the interiors. During the 1947 restoration, the stucco decoration was restored, and the column and pediment were reconstructed.
